text: Your engineer says, use M twenty. What does that actually mean?
M stands for mix. The number is the strength grade of the concrete.
Small cubes of the concrete are tested, and the grade tells you the strength it is designed to reach.
A higher number means a stronger mix, and usually a higher cost.
Your engineer picks the grade for each part of the house, based on the design.
But on site, the grade only holds if the mix is right. Cement, sand, aggregate and water, in the right amounts.
Extra water makes it easier to pour, but weaker.
So ask your engineer which grade goes where, and how the mix will be checked on site.
Send this to someone who is building.
